sourceCommitNote: Source fixes compiled for the isolated localhost walkthrough. The final package-boundary refactor preserves the manually observed emitted browser binding.
runtime: Isolated localhost; browser email/password login enabled; SSO off; deterministic local AI provider
method: Manual browser walkthrough with explicitly labelled browser HTTP 503 and response-delay injections

issues.title: Search exposes results from the previous query
issues.problem: Changing the query retained old clickable results during the debounce window; an earlier in-flight response could replace results for the new text.
issues.change: Abort the old request immediately, clear its results, and accept responses only for the current query.
issues.result: With a manually delayed local response, changing the query immediately removed the old results and showed the pending search.

issues.title: Failed chat rename loses the entered name
issues.problem: A rejected Rename discarded the typed title and switched away from the Rename dialog.
issues.change: Retain the Rename action and typed title after a failure, show its error, and allow an explicit retry.
issues.result: A manually injected local HTTP 503 retained the name. Retrying Rename succeeded with that name.

issues.title: Stop fails silently during a running response
issues.problem: A failed Stop request left the response running without explaining the failure.
issues.change: Show a Stop-specific failure beside the composer and restore the Stop action for retry.
issues.result: A manually injected local HTTP 503 showed a visible Stop-specific alert during a running response. Retrying Stop succeeded and the running-response controls disappeared. No page errors were observed in that recovery flow.
issues.injection: Browser HTTP 503 interception; deterministic local AI response

issues.title: Failed saved-query operation leaves Saving stuck
issues.problem: A failed Save left the pending label and disabled controls without a useful recovery path.
issues.change: Show the transport failure, retain the query draft and the original operation identity, and allow an explicit retry when the outcome is unknown.
issues.result: A manually injected local HTTP 503 preserved the draft and exposed retry. Retrying the same operation succeeded without an extra copy.

issues.title: Enter submits raw @context text while lookup is pending
issues.problem: Pressing Enter during a pending context lookup sent the raw @query as a chat message instead of waiting for context selection.
issues.change: Separate the browser’s pending lookup request from server-returned search results. Enter waits while lookup is pending; a failed current request offers Retry search, which retries that context query.
issues.result: Enter during a delayed context lookup retained the draft and made no chat-turn request. A manually injected local HTTP 503 exposed Retry search; retry returned permitted dashboard and semantic-model options. Selecting a permitted semantic model added its context chip.
issues.status: Manually observed locally after the final context change
issues.injection: Browser response delay and HTTP 503 interception

sourceHardenings.title: Favorites and Last opened belong to the signed-in principal
sourceHardenings.problem: Browser-wide preference keys could attribute one account’s favorites and recents to another account.
sourceHardenings.change: Catalog and dashboard report use the same canonical-principal-scoped favorite key; recents are scoped as well. Legacy keys remain untouched but unused because their owner is unknown.
sourceHardenings.result: A scoped browser storage key and the current account’s Favorites view were observed. A two-account walkthrough in the same browser was not obtained.
sourceHardenings.migration: One-time Favorites and Last opened reset; no legacy ownership is inferred.

sourceHardenings.title: Saved-query mutation controls use current server capabilities
sourceHardenings.problem: Shared saved-query controls must not infer mutation authority from visibility or a role label.
sourceHardenings.change: Project canEdit and canArchive through the same lifecycle authorizer as mutations. The UI shows Save changes and Archive only for the permitted current actor. Server mutations still independently reauthorize.
sourceHardenings.result: The valid owner retained Save changes, Duplicate and Archive, and owner save/archive actions worked. Nonowner runtime proof was not obtained: the database rejected an attempted owner reassignment through its immutable identity trigger, and that protection was not bypassed.
sourceHardenings.status: Source hardening; owner path observed; nonowner path unverified

limits: Browser email/password login is enabled; SSO is off. PR #1016 remains unmerged. No production configuration, release or merge is claimed.
AI interactions used a deterministic local provider. Production AI connectivity, reasoning quality and autonomous dashboard generation remain unverified.
A live Microsoft/Azure tenant login, consent, MFA and Conditional Access were not verified. Optional Microsoft SSO support is not an enabled rollout in this walkthrough.
Payment or subscription behavior was not verified.
HTTP 503 failures and response delays were deliberately injected in the local browser to reproduce recovery behavior; they are not evidence of production outages.

Nonowner saved-query mutation behavior was source-reviewed but not proven at runtime. The immutable database owner-identity protection rejected the attempted fixture reassignment; no mutation occurred and the protection was not bypassed.
A principal-scoped browser preference key was observed, but two accounts in one browser were not walked through. Unknown-owner legacy preferences are intentionally not migrated.
No new test cases, automated tests, CI, typechecks, URI checks or automated check passes were run for this walkthrough. Manual local browser evidence has the limits described here.
